sigObserver.rootCause: SIG's shred_receiver read the snapshot slot then DISCARDED it (_ = slot; // TODO), and Receiver.updateSlotRange was never called, so root_slot stayed 0 and max_slot stayed maxInt(Slot) — every shred was accepted. In a cluster racing ahead of the snapshot, live-tip turbine shreds form merkle trees that never connect to the snapshot root (orphans); replay's merkle forest is a FIXED 4096-node pool with NO eviction (services/replay.zig:78 documents this), so orphans filled it and replay exited error.OutOfSpace.
sigObserver.fix: v2/services/shred_receiver.zig (deviation 5, commit f4ccc97c): call the existing updateSlotRange(snapshot_slot, snapshot_slot + 96) so only the contiguous window the snapshot base can root is accepted; shreds outside it are rejected via the existing ShredOlderThanRoot/ShredTooNew filters instead of accumulating as orphans.
sigObserver.verified: SIG stayed ALIVE with 0 OutOfSpace; replay completed real slots (e.g. 186, 211); it appears in a peer's gossip view (gossipNodes=3).
sigObserver.honestAssessment: joined — SIG appeared in the shared-genesis gossip view (read from a PEER, the bootstrap). SIG is a NON-VOTING observer (no vote/stake accounts — structurally impossible); it never votes. The 20-slot target is met by the two voting validators. This is a TWO-voting-validator-plus-one-SIG-observer run, NOT a three-voting-validator or five-client testnet.
